todays_goal: Finish the Peloponnesian War sequence with Sparta's naval adaptation, Persian support, Aegospotami, and Athens's surrender.

lessons.subject: history_geography
lessons.previous_learning: Atticus understands why the Sicilian Expedition was a turning point and how it weakened Athens.
lessons.course_context: Complete the war sequence by explaining Sparta's naval adaptation, Persian support, Aegospotami, and Athens's surrender.
learning_objectives: Explain why Sparta needed naval power.
Explain how Persian funding helped Sparta.
Explain why Athens's fleet loss mattered.
lessons.why_it_matters: The end of the war shows how strategy, resources, and adaptation can change a long conflict.

vocabulary.definition: the 405 BCE battle where Sparta destroyed much of the Athenian fleet
the Spartan commander linked to Sparta's final naval victory

lessons.written_instruction: Atticus: Sicily weakened Athens, but the war continued. Persian financial support helped Sparta build stronger naval power. Sparta defeated the Athenian fleet at Aegospotami in 405 BCE. Athens surrendered in 404 BCE.

worked_examples.title: Cause chain
worked_examples.solution: Sicily -> Persian support -> stronger Spartan navy -> Aegospotami -> surrender
worked_examples.explanation: Sparta adapted to challenge Athens at sea.

independent_practice.prompt: Why did Sparta need a stronger navy?
How did Persian money help Sparta?
Why was losing the fleet serious for Athens?
Put the final events in order.

exit_ticket.prompt: In 4 sentences, explain how Sparta changed its strategy and why that helped end the war.
exit_ticket.answer: Mention naval adaptation, Persian support, Aegospotami, and Athens's inability to keep fighting.

lessons.voice_prompt: Teach the sequence before questions. Use a five-box cause chain. Keep wording concrete and age-appropriate. Focus on documented strategy, resources, and outcomes.
lessons.teacher_notes: Historical facts checked against World History Encyclopedia.
